ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identity adapter for a native 3D generator from one reference image
PROPOSAL: Attach a cross-attention adapter to a pretrained native 3D generator such as TRELLIS, feeding it DINOv2 patch features of the reference photo at each transformer block so that colour and markings come from the subject rather than from the generator's prior. Train the adapter on rendered Objaverse objects with the reference taken from a random view, then personalise to unseen subjects with a few hundred optimisation steps.
CONTROLS: The unmodified generator, an IP-Adapter-style CLIP injection, texture projection of the reference onto the front view, and ablations removing the DINOv2 features or the per-block injection; three seeds, with DINOv2 and CLIP image score on side and back renders, plus a user ranking.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Identity score on unseen views should rise clearly over the base generator; it may fail for subjects with patterns visible only from the back, where no feature of the reference constrains them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-view diffusion finetuning with an identity loss on 3D renders
PROPOSAL: Finetune Zero123++ on Objaverse and CO3Dv2 with an identity loss computed between DINOv2 features of generated novel views and of the reference, training a second adapter variant per of three base models with seven loss weights and three seeds. Distil each finetuned model into a Gaussian splatting reconstruction, and render forty held-out viewpoints per subject for evaluation on side and back renders, logging the identity score per camera elevation and azimuth bin.
CONTROLS: Base Zero123++, a DreamBooth-style finetune per subject, a CLIP-only loss, and ablations removing the identity loss and the distillation step, run on all three base models with a user ranking of the renders and a failure inspection of the worst decile.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The identity loss should reduce colour drift on unseen views; it may fail when the base model's systematic bias is stronger than the loss signal, leaving a bluish tone on the back.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Subject token with low-rank tuning of a multi-view diffusion model
PROPOSAL: Bind a rare text token to the subject by low-rank tuning of MVDream on the single reference image plus synthetic variants (colour jitter, background changes, small rotations), with prior-preservation images generated by the base model. Lift the four generated views to 3D with an off-the-shelf reconstruction network and compare identity on the back and side views of the result.
CONTROLS: Base MVDream with the plain caption, a token-only embedding optimisation, full finetuning of the network, and a run without prior-preservation images; five subjects from the DreamBooth set and three seeds, scored by CLIP and DINOv2 similarity of side and back views.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Low-rank tuning should retain more identity than token-only optimisation at modest cost; it may fail by overfitting to the front view, giving a pasted look on the back.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-model personalisation study over images, videos and renders
PROPOSAL: Compare four personalisation strategies (token optimisation, low-rank tuning, full finetuning, adapter injection) on three base models, MVDream, SV3D and Hunyuan3D, using thirty subjects drawn from the DreamBooth, CO3Dv2 and a set of Blender turntable renders. Train each combination with three seeds and three learning rates, then evaluate identity on twelve views per subject, including side and back views, and break the scores down by subject category and by base model.
CONTROLS: Base models without personalisation, and for the four strategies an ablation with the reference image removed from conditioning, plus a variant trained with twice the number of augmentations and a CLIP-based scorer on every rendered view of each subject.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Low-rank tuning should land near the best strategy on most base models; the comparison may fail to separate strategies when variance among subjects dominates the differences.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Canonical-space 4D Gaussians with identity distillation from a video model
PROPOSAL: Fit a canonical set of 3D Gaussians plus a deformation field to the input video of the subject, supervising novel views through a video diffusion prior personalised on the video frames with low-rank tuning. A DINOv2 identity loss ties the rendered side and back views to features of the input frames, and a temporal smoothness term on the deformation field keeps motion coherent over 32 frames.
CONTROLS: Consistent4D and a deformation-only variant without personalisation, score distillation from an unpersonalised video prior, and ablations removing the identity loss and the smoothness term; three seeds on the Consistent4D benchmark videos and 20 self-collected clips, with LPIPS, CLIP and DINOv2 scores.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Identity scores on unseen views should improve over the unpersonalised prior; the method may fail to handle fast non-rigid motion, because the canonical space cannot explain the deformation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-clip optimisation with personalised video priors and long schedules
PROPOSAL: Run the 4D pipeline with five personalised video priors, built by low-rank tuning on the input clip with different token initialisations, and optimise the canonical Gaussians for 30000 steps per prior on 32-frame clips from the Consistent4D and 20 collected videos. Combine the resulting assets by averaging their colour fields, and render sixteen novel views per frame to measure identity and temporal consistency on side and back renders, with per-clip curves of identity over the optimisation steps.
CONTROLS: Single-prior optimisation, an unpersonalised prior, and a variant without the averaging of colour fields; ablations on step counts of 3000, 10000 and 30000, scored by DINOv2, CLIP and a flicker measure over three seeds.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Averaging priors should reduce view-dependent colour error; it may not beat a single well-chosen prior once the optimisation schedule is long, since the priors then converge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Texture-space colour correction guided by the reference
PROPOSAL: Generate a mesh with an off-the-shelf image-to-3D model, then fit a correction map in UV space that matches the colour histogram and local patches of the reference on the visible side and propagates them to occluded regions through a small convolutional network trained on Objaverse textures. The correction runs once per asset and needs no diffusion sampling.
CONTROLS: The uncorrected mesh texture, global histogram matching, a front-view projection without propagation, and a network without patch matching; three seeds, scored by DINOv2 similarity of side and back views and by user preference on 40 subjects.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: UV propagation should remove bluish or washed-out tones on the back at low runtime; it may fail on subjects with asymmetric patterns, when propagated colours are wrong.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identity-aware selection among reference-conditioned 3D generators
PROPOSAL: Pair five image-to-3D generators with three reference encoders (CLIP, DINOv2, SigLIP) and run each pair on sixty subjects from the CO3Dv2 and DreamBooth, with six guidance strengths, choosing per subject the output with the highest identity score on rendered back views. Report the gain of selection over the single best generator per encoder, and the agreement between encoders on side and back views.
CONTROLS: Each generator without selection, random selection among the five, and a selection score based on front-view similarity only; ablations on the number of candidates retained, using three seeds and a user check on forty subjects.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Selection should raise the average identity score over any single generator; it may fail because the identity scorer shares errors with the encoder used for conditioning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-time optimisation of a texture latent against reference features
PROPOSAL: Keep a pretrained native 3D generator fixed and optimise only its texture latent for each subject so the front renders match the reference, while a DINOv2 feature loss on side and back renders limits drift from the reference identity. Use 12 random viewpoints per step for 400 steps, and an exponential moving average of the latent for stability.
CONTROLS: The generator's default output, projection of the reference onto the mesh, optimisation without the feature loss, and optimisation of the full latent instead of the texture part; three seeds on 25 subjects, measuring DINOv2 and CLIP score and geometry drift via Chamfer distance.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: Optimising only the texture latent should improve identity while leaving geometry nearly unchanged; it may fail on subjects whose identity is geometric, such as unusual body shapes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Supervised identity data from rendered turntables
PROPOSAL: Render 8000 Objaverse objects on turntables under seven lighting setups, and train an image-to-3D model with reference conditioning on random pairs of views, using three data sizes and two architectures with three seeds, then log the identity score of each checkpoint on held-out subjects to show how it grows with data. Evaluate on CO3Dv2 and DreamBooth subjects with 16 held-out views covering side and back, and compare with the same models trained without lighting variation.
CONTROLS: The pretrained generator without our data, finetuning on real CO3Dv2 captures only, and ablations on the number of lighting setups and of view pairs per object, scored by DINOv2 and CLIP similarity.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: Rendered turntables should teach consistent colour between views; the gain may fail to transfer to real photographs because of the domain gap in lighting and materials.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reference-conditioned score distillation with identity guidance
PROPOSAL: Optimise a NeRF for the subject with score distillation from a personalised Stable Diffusion model, tuned on the reference image with low-rank adaptation, and add a guidance term pushing DINOv2 features of side and back views toward those of the reference. Use a coarse-to-fine camera schedule with 3 elevation bands and a shared background so colour is not averaged out.
CONTROLS: Standard distillation from the unpersonalised model, distillation from the personalised model alone, and a variant with the identity term only; three seeds, 15 DreamBooth subjects, scored with CLIP and DINOv2 similarity on 12 views and by a user ranking.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The identity guidance should reduce averaging of colours on unseen views; it may fail through over-saturated renders when the guidance weight dominates the diffusion score.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Choosing reference encoders as identity scorers for 3D assets
PROPOSAL: Evaluate six reference encoders (two CLIP variants, two DINOv2 variants, SigLIP, a re-identification network) as identity scorers for generated 3D assets, rendered from 24 cameras around 40 subjects, and train a guidance variant per encoder with three weights on top of a native generator. Report rank correlation with a study of 12 raters, split by side and back views and by subject category, and a bootstrap interval per correlation.
CONTROLS: A generator without guidance, random guidance directions, and for the six encoders a variant scoring the front view only; ablations on the camera count, over three seeds.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: DINOv2 scorers should correlate best with raters on back views; the study may not rank encoders when raters weigh colour above shape.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint video and multi-view prior personalisation for subject-driven 4D assets
PROPOSAL: Personalise a video diffusion model and a multi-view diffusion model together on the subject video with shared low-rank adapters, so both priors agree about the subject's colour and markings, and alternate them to supervise a deformable Gaussian representation. Train on 24-frame clips of animals and objects from Consistent4D and captured videos, with a final identity-aware refinement stage on rendered side and back views.
CONTROLS: Separate personalisation of each prior, personalisation of one prior only, an unpersonalised pipeline, and a model without alternation; three seeds, scored by DINOv2 identity score, CLIP and temporal consistency of renders.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Shared adapters should give more consistent identity between viewpoints than separate ones; they may fail if the video prior's motion bias overrides the multi-view prior's colours.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Search over personalisation recipes for 4D generation
PROPOSAL: Search personalisation recipes for 4D assets: six adapter ranks, five learning rates, eight identity loss weights and three token schemes, giving 360 configurations, each trained on a short Consistent4D clip and rated at twenty viewpoints on side and back renders. Retain the best twenty-eight configurations, train them on forty more clips, then fit a surrogate model of identity score from configuration features.
CONTROLS: A default recipe, random search with matched trials, and the best recipe trained without the identity loss; ablations on the clip count in the final stage, scored by DINOv2 and CLIP using three seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: A tuned recipe should beat the default on identity similarity by a clear amount; the search may be unable to generalise to new clips, with the best configuration varying by clip.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reference memory for image-to-3D personalisation
PROPOSAL: Keep a native 3D generator frozen and add a small memory module which stores DINOv2 tokens of the reference and is queried by the denoising blocks, trained on Objaverse renders with random reference views. Evaluate against reference photos from DreamBooth and CO3Dv2 and compare identity on side and back views of the generated meshes with 16 viewpoints per subject.
CONTROLS: The frozen generator without memory, a CLIP-based conditioning variant, a front-projection baseline, and ablations on the memory size and the number of queried blocks; three seeds, DINOv2 and CLIP similarity.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: A reference memory should improve colour fidelity on occluded views at low training expense; it may fail when the reference shows the subject in a rare pose which the memory encodes poorly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Video-to-4D identity transfer with long refinement runs
PROPOSAL: Run three video-to-4D pipelines (Consistent4D, STAG4D, a native 4D generator) on thirty clips, each followed by an identity refinement stage of 20000 steps with six loss weights, and render twenty-six viewpoints per frame at sixteen frames to score identity and temporal consistency on side and back views with DINOv2, CLIP and a flow-based flicker measure.
CONTROLS: The same pipelines without refinement, a refinement with a 2D identity loss only, and a refinement of 2000 steps; ablations on loss weights per pipeline, with three seeds.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Refinement should improve identity per pipeline; the gain may fail to survive beyond short clips because flicker grows with the refinement length.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Native 4D personalisation with identity-conditioned deformation
PROPOSAL: Train a deformation module on top of a pretrained native 4D generator, conditioned on DINOv2 tokens of the input video frames, to keep colours of unseen views tied to the subject while it moves. Supervision comes from rendered 4D sequences of Objaverse animated assets, with the reference video taken from a random view, and personalisation to a new subject takes a short finetune.
CONTROLS: The unmodified generator, a CLIP-conditioned variant, a frame-averaging baseline, and ablations removing the deformation conditioning and the animated pretraining; three seeds on Consistent4D videos and 20 captured clips, with DINOv2, CLIP and temporal consistency scores.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Identity-conditioned deformation should lower colour drift on side and back views during motion; it may fail on animal species absent from the animated pretraining set.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalised 4D asset study over priors, strategies and schedules
PROPOSAL: Evaluate three priors (video, multi-view, native 4D), four personalisation strategies and three step schedules on 24 clips from the Consistent4D and 16 collected videos, training each of the thirty-six combinations over three seeds and rendering 20 viewpoints per frame for identity and temporal consistency on side and back renders, then fit a mixed-effects model to attribute variance to each factor, with subject category as a random term.
CONTROLS: An unpersonalised pipeline per prior, and ablations removing the identity loss and the temporal term; scored by DINOv2, CLIP and a flicker measure on all combinations.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The prior should explain most variance in identity scores; the model may not separate strategies when clips are few relative to the number of factors.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Image-to-3D personalisation with an identity critic and rejection sampling
PROPOSAL: Train a small identity critic on Objaverse renders that predicts DINOv2 similarity between a reference and a rendered novel view from features of the generator's intermediate latents, then draw candidates from a native generator and keep the one the critic ranks first. Evaluate on DreamBooth and CO3Dv2 subjects with 16 viewpoints, focusing on side and back views.
CONTROLS: The generator's single sample, random choice among candidates, selection by CLIP similarity on the front view, and ablations on the number of candidates and critic input; three seeds, DINOv2 and CLIP similarity.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Critic-based selection should improve identity at small training expense; it may fail because candidates share the same colour bias, leaving no good option to pick.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identity refinement of 4D assets with dense camera coverage
PROPOSAL: Refine generated 4D assets with a personalised image prior on 40 videos, rendering 48 cameras per frame at eight timesteps and supervising each render with a DINOv2 identity loss, then compare identity on side and back views with the unrefined asset. Use 5000 refinement steps and three loss weights, and report temporal consistency with a flow-based flicker measure.
CONTROLS: The unrefined asset, refinement with six cameras, refinement without temporal term, and an image prior without personalisation; scored by DINOv2 and CLIP, using three seeds on all variants.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Dense camera coverage should improve back-view identity; the gain may be unable to exceed that of the 6-camera variant, indicating that most of the benefit comes from the loss rather than coverage.
